Yes, communication disorders can indeed extend to musical messages. The primary therapeutic tool in music therapy sessions focuses on conveying emotions or movements through music, which may be decoded differently by persons with different types of communication disorders. This means that individuals with various communication conditions, such as apraxia, dysarthria, or autism spectrum disorder, might have unique challenges when engaging with musical messages.

When selecting music for clinical interventions focusing on emotions or movement, clinicians should consider the differential abilities and preferences of individuals with these communication disorders. By doing so, they can provide more effective and personalized treatment, which may lead to better outcomes and improved quality of life for those affected.

It's essential to note that not all individuals with communication disorders will benefit from music therapy, and some might require alternative interventions. However, when used in conjunction with other therapeutic approaches, music therapy can be a valuable tool in supporting the recovery and well-being of people with various communication conditions.
